yt_cranberry_meadows.blurb: Cranberry Meadows is one of the pockets of granite inside Golden Canyon, a short drive from Whitehorse along the Takhini River road. It holds a small collection of single-pitch lines, mostly trad with four sport routes mixed in. Grades start around 5.7 and run up to the low 5.11s, but the bulk of the climbs sit in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, which makes it a fair stop for a leader with a moderate rack and a few clips. The face sits in sun for most of the day, and the canyon around it is quiet and scenic.

_expect.name: The Point Buttress (Main Wall) aka Overlook

tn_the_point_buttress_main_wall_aka_over.blurb: The Point Buttress is a wall at Castle Rock, the orange bluff above the town of Jasper, Tennessee. Almost all of its thirteen lines are bolted sport climbs, with one trad route, and the grades cluster from 5.10 into the 5.11s with a couple of easier options near 5.7 and 5.8. The angle is a little gentler than elsewhere on the bluff, and the climbing leans on blocky features, edges and technical movement. That makes it a popular place to warm up before heading to the steeper walls, and it can fill up early in the day.

nh_mir_summit_kiosk_boulders.blurb: This cluster of boulders sits beside the park's fire road, across from Round Pond in Pawtuckaway State Park, on the Hillside side of the park in southern New Hampshire. Eleven of the thirteen routes are boulder problems, running from an easy V0 up through the V3 to V8 range with a couple of V8-V9 sit-start tests, and there are two short trad lines as well. The Mir and Summit boulders are big, and the Kiosk marks the way in. Hillside boulders are mostly shaded and tend to be uncrowded.

nv_three_peaks_cliff.blurb: Three Peaks Cliff is the main formation on the west side of Three Peaks Gully, on the west shoulder of Kraft Mountain above Calico Basin in Red Rock, Nevada. Most of its thirteen routes are trad, with a few top-rope lines, and the difficulty is gentle: mostly 5.4 to 5.7, plus one 5.9 and one 5.10. Faces point both south-west and south-east, so sun reaches the south-west lines from late morning and the south-east lines through the early afternoon. It rarely sees other climbers, making it a quiet pick for newer leaders.

az_wave_wall_aka_widowmaker.blurb: Wave Wall is a bouldering wall near Lake Mary outside Flagstaff, Arizona, at roughly 7,000 feet, next to the Workshop Wall. It has thirteen problems and is mainly a warm-up venue for the harder boulders nearby: most are V0 to V2, with a single V6 standing well apart from the rest. Expect good landings, small bulges and deep pockets. Take care on the descent near one of the lines, which can be tricky.

ar_mount_sequoyah_bouldering.blurb: Mount Sequoyah Bouldering is a south-facing band of sandstone on the hillside above Fayetteville, in northwest Arkansas. Twelve problems are described, spanning a vertical to overhanging style: one VB and a few V1s, then a cluster at V3 with a couple of harder lines at V4 and V5. The wall sits in shade and overhangs, so it seeps after rain and can take days to dry out. A few suspect blocks on the right side are best avoided.

ar_brick_attack_area.blurb: Brick Attack Area is a stretch of Cave Creek, in the Sam's Throne zone of north-central Arkansas, and gathers some of the creek's best-known lines on sandstone. Nine of the twelve routes are bolted sport climbs, with three trad lines, and the difficulty is hard-leaning: mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a single 5.8 trad route. To get there, take the usual way down from the top, then turn left and walk until you reach a prominent roof.
